card.name: Limbo
card.tagline: Trinidad's iconic backbend-under-the-bar dance — born from funeral wake tradition, conquered global beach resorts worldwide.
card.profile: Limbo is Trinidad and Tobago's most internationally famous dance — the contortionist art of bending backwards to pass beneath a horizontal bar that is progressively lowered. Originating in the 19th century post-emancipation Trinidad as part of African-Caribbean funeral wake celebrations (some scholars trace it to the symbolic passage of souls through the underworld), limbo was popularised worldwide by Trinidadian dancer Julia Edwards in the 1950s and 1960s. Today limbo is a fixture of Caribbean cultural performance, Carnival celebrations, and global beach resort entertainment, though the form retains its serious Trinidadian roots.
card.insight: According to a 1956 newspaper report, the game was revived in 1944 by Edric Connor. A film, Julia and Joyce, by Trinidadian-American Sonja Dumas, was released in 2010. == World record == The world record for lowest limbo game is held by Dennis Walston, who successfully attempted a 6-inch bar in March 1991.
